Al Jazeera, News, Child Rights. LD datePublished = dateModified Thu 15 Oct 05:43 BST. No named byline (organisation-attributed).
Headline: 'Israel has detained more than 2,000 Palestinian children since 2023: report'.
SOURCE OF THE CLAIM: the Palestinian Prisoner's Society, a Palestinian rights group, in a report released on Wednesday. Israeli forces have detained more than 2,000 Palestinian children since October 2023. At least 350 Palestinian children currently face 'harsh conditions' in Israeli prisons.
On Tuesday, Israeli forces arrested at least six children from Hebron in the occupied West Bank, the report said.
The group said information on the number of children arrested in Gaza is unclear given thousands of missing persons, including children, and the ongoing policy of enforced disappearance.
The group said Israel's policy of detention without charges or a release date constitutes 'an additional violation and crime that leaves children facing the unknown and deprives them of family and educational stability'. The report described practices beginning with 'intimidation and arrest' and extending to 'torture, starvation and denial of healthcare'.
CASES: Mohammed Hamid, 15, contracted scabies while detained in Ofer Prison, suffered severe infections, underwent heart surgery, was admitted to intensive care in critical condition and subsequently had one of his legs amputated. Walid Ahmed, 17, died in March 2025 after six months in Megiddo Prison; in December an Israeli judge halted the investigation into his death, stating that although there was evidence of starvation, no definitive cause of death had been established. Ahmed was imprisoned with Mohammed Ibrahim, a teenager from Florida, released after months of advocacy from US-based organisations and appeals from high-ranking lawmakers. Abdalkareem Issa Ahmed Safi, also a young American, was reportedly taken from his West Bank home in a late-night raid in June, turned 18 in detention and was moved from a youth holding area into an adult section at Ofer Prison.
SINGLE-SOURCED AND ADVOCACY-SOURCED: one approved outlet (Al Jazeera) reporting one campaign group's report. No Israeli government response is carried in the piece and no independent corroboration. If used, attribute explicitly to the Palestinian Prisoner's Society and note the absence of an Israeli response.
RELATED AND STRONGER ON SOURCING: BBC Verify's own investigation, 'Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings without public outcome, BBC Verify finds', https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c574e228vlygo - BBC's own reporting rather than a wire pickup or a group's report.
